title: The Mill and the Machine: from a converted watermill in Thuringia to an institute for machine consciousness
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Weimar, the birth in the German Democratic Republic
stops.date_confidence: Year and city attested and corroborated across sources; the day and month are universally repeated but no civil record standing behind them has been produced, so 21 December is carried on report rather than on document.
stops.campa: Weimar in the German Democratic Republic, a town of classical ghosts and prefabricated housing blocks, registers a birth in the last week of December. His mother's family are Communist politicians, and she can hold the party's ideology and its domestic failure in mind at the same time. His father is an architect who resists the political climate he lives in while admitting that socialism has made his own economic security possible. The child is born into a house that holds both positions at once and does not resolve them.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The civic registers of Weimar, GDR, December 1973; no birth record has been produced publicly

stops.name: The countryside southeast of Weimar, the mill converted
stops.date_confidence: The conversion is attested by Musser's profile from Bach's own account; no year is given and 1978 is an ordering device. The site itself is unpublished, so the coordinate is an approximate point over farmland southeast of Weimar and not a confirmed location.
stops.campa: His parents, both architecture students, buy an old mill in the countryside southeast of Weimar and refuse the standardized design the Eastern Bloc supplies. They turn it into what a visitor will later call an arcadia of sculpture gardens and concert nooks. Where exactly it stands is not published; the point on the map is a few kilometres of guesswork over farmland. What is not guesswork is the principle, a house built against the official pattern book in a country where the pattern book had the force of law.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The unlocated mill house southeast of Weimar, with its sculpture gardens and concert nooks

stops.name: The mill, the wall that became a door
stops.date_confidence: The anecdote is attested verbatim in Musser's profile and undated; 1982 is an ordering device placing it inside Bach's childhood at the mill.
stops.campa: The father works on the mill the way a man works on a sentence he is not yet finished with. He begins hammering a doorway through a wall while still in his pyjamas, having decided over breakfast that the wall was wrong. The boy watches from the table. Decades later, describing minds as models a system generates and then revises, he will not have to reach far for the image of a structure edited from inside while the people are still living in it. There are no neighbours close enough to object to the noise.
stops.quote: My father would sometimes get up at the breakfast table staring at a wall, deciding that it would be a door instead.
stops.quote_source: Joscha Bach, quoted in George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The doorways of the mill, cut by an architect in his pyjamas

stops.name: The mill, the Commodore 64 and no one to play with
stops.date_confidence: Attested in Musser's profile as a childhood practice with no year given; 1985 is an ordering device. No surviving childhood code has been located.
stops.campa: There are no other children at the mill. Bach has a Commodore 64 and nobody to play with, so he writes the players: variants of Parcheesi, a version of Missile Command, board games and arcade games rebuilt as code because code will sit down opposite him. He reads philosophy in the same rooms. The isolation is not reported as a hardship; it is simply the arrangement, an artistically furnished house in the Thuringian countryside with one child in it and a machine that answers. None of the code survives in any archive anyone has found.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The Commodore 64 game variants written at the mill; no code survives in any public archive

stops.name: Weimar, school ends as the state does
stops.date_confidence: Attested only in Musser's profile, which says he finished high school as the Berlin Wall fell; neither school nor examination date is published. Note an unresolved strain: a December 1973 birth makes him fifteen that November, early for a German Abitur, and no source addresses it.
stops.campa: He finishes secondary school in the months when the country he was born in stops existing. Neither the school nor the examination date appears in any published source; what is recorded is the coincidence, that the certificate and the border came loose in the same season. East Germany had a future assigned for him, the placement of a bright pupil into a planned economy's slot. The assignment lapses before it can be applied. By the birth date everyone repeats he is fifteen that November, early for an Abitur, and no source addresses it.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The opening of the inner German border, 9 November 1989

stops.name: North America, three thousand miles on a recumbent bicycle
stops.date_confidence: The ride is attested in Musser's profile, placed after school and before university; route, entry points, and dates are unpublished. The coordinate is a nominal mid-continent placeholder, not a stop he is known to have made.
stops.campa: He builds a recumbent bicycle and rides it more than three thousand miles across the United States and Canada. No route survives, no dates, no entry point; the coordinate here is a placeholder in the middle of a continent and stands for nothing except the fact of the crossing. A boy raised inside a walled country, handed the world in a single year, answers by lying back on a frame he welded himself and pedalling until the distance is used up. The mill is an ocean and half a continent behind him.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The recumbent bicycle Bach built himself; no photograph or route log has been published

stops.name: Hamilton, the year abroad and the compression course
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. Musser's profile confirms a year abroad and a text-compression course that changed his understanding of cognition, but names neither country nor university; the University of Waikato comes from the dossier alone and is not in en.wikipedia either. The coordinate verifies at 0.48 km from Waikato if the claim is right.
stops.campa: Somewhere in a year spent studying abroad, Bach takes a course in text compression, and it rearranges what he thinks a mind is. Intelligence stops looking like a list of facts and starts looking like the shortest program that can regenerate them. The dossier places this at the University of Waikato in New Zealand; the profile that carries the anecdote names neither the country nor the university. The idea is the durable part. He will spend thirty years arguing that a self is a compression too, and a lossy one.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018 (year abroad and compression course, university unnamed)
suggested_refs: Ian Witten's text-compression group at the University of Waikato, the dossier's proposed setting

stops.name: Berlin, Humboldt University and two subjects at once
stops.date_confidence: Attested as to institution and fields by en.wikipedia; the start year is not published and 1996 is an ordering device working back from a degree completed around 2000.
stops.campa: He returns to Berlin and enrols at Humboldt, taking computer science and philosophy together rather than choosing between them. He studies the two subjects as though they were one subject, and everything he publishes afterward works at making the seam between them invisible. The building on Unter den Linden was a Prussian prince's palace before it was a university, and it stands in what was, until he was fifteen, the capital of the state his father resented.
suggested_refs: The main building of Humboldt University, Unter den Linden 6, Berlin

stops.name: Berlin, the birthday party
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The meeting is a dossier detail giving only the city; venue and year are unpublished and the source chain is thin. The date is an ordering device. The quotation itself is verbatim from Musser and independent of the meeting story.
stops.campa: At a birthday party in Berlin he meets the artist he will marry. The venue is not published and neither is the year, and the source is thin enough that the whole scene should be read as tradition rather than record. What is on the record is how he describes the pair of them afterward, inside a taxonomy of temperaments, Elves and Orcs, that he applies to everyone he meets and to institutions as readily as to people. He is still using it in interviews twenty years later. He is not being whimsical about it.
stops.quote: People like me and my wife are basically Elves.
stops.quote_source: Joscha Bach to George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018. The printed text continues after narration: 'We are dreamers. We live to sing and dance and create palaces in our minds.'
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: Bach's Elves and Orcs typology, recurring across his interviews and lectures

stops.name: Berlin, the degree and the entropy models
stops.date_confidence: Year attested by en.wikipedia. The qualification is rendered variously as an M.A. and as a German Diplom across sources and no transcript settles it; the variance is left standing. The 2001 paper is carried from the dossier bibliography and was not independently fetched.
stops.campa: He finishes at Humboldt in 2000. Sources render the qualification variously, an M.A. in one place and a German Diplom in another, and nothing available settles it. The following year he publishes on supporting textual input by using multiple entropy models, the compression course from the year abroad surfacing at last as an actual paper. He is twenty-six. He has crossed a continent on a bicycle and has not yet built the architecture that will carry his name for the next two decades.
sources: Dossier bibliography: 'Supporting Textual Input by Using Multiple Entropy Models' (2001)
suggested_refs: 'Supporting Textual Input by Using Multiple Entropy Models', 2001

segments.name: Osnabrück: The Architecture of Motivated Cognition

stops.name: Osnabrück, the Institute of Cognitive Science
stops.date_confidence: The three advisers are attested in the en.wikipedia infobox; the start year is not published and 2001 orders the segment. Coordinate corrected: the pool gave 52.2705, 8.0553, which is 2.07 km southeast of Wachsbleiche 27; the address geocodes to approximately 52.2852, 8.0366.
stops.campa: At the Institute of Cognitive Science in Osnabrück he works under Dietrich Dörner, Kai-Uwe Kühnberger, and Hans-Dieter Burkhard. Dörner has spent decades on Psi, a theory that treats cognition as driven by needs and motives rather than by inference alone: a mind that gets hungry, that gets bored, that acts because something inside it is out of balance. Bach's contribution is to build it. MicroPsi is the implementation: node nets in which a drive rises, competes with the other drives, and is what makes the reasoning start at all.
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Joscha Bach' (infobox: doctoral advisers Dörner, Kühnberger, Burkhard)
suggested_refs: Dietrich Dörner's Psi theory of motivated cognition, the direct ancestor of MicroPsi

stops.name: Osnabrück, the node nets published with Ronnie Vuine
stops.date_confidence: The paper is attested in DBLP: Bach and Vuine, 'Designing Agents with MicroPsi Node Nets', KI 2003 proceedings, pp. 164-178. The conference city is not established by any source fetched, so the stop sits at Bach's own institute rather than at an assumed venue, and the month orders the segment.
stops.campa: With Ronnie Vuine he publishes 'Designing Agents with MicroPsi Node Nets' in the proceedings of the German AI conference, the architecture's first public presentation. The agents have drives. They explore, they get frustrated, they form representations because a representation serves an appetite. The paper is short and the trail of citations out of it is long. Vuine will still be beside him eleven years later, when the two of them turn the same mathematics on industrial robot arms in Berlin.
sources: DBLP, KI 2003 proceedings record (Bach and Vuine, pp. 164-178)
suggested_refs: 'Designing Agents with MicroPsi Node Nets', KI 2003, pp. 164-178

stops.name: Osnabrück, the doctorate in cognitive science
stops.date_confidence: Contradiction left standing. Both en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia give the PhD as 2006; the dossier gives the dissertation as publicly dated March 2007. The Osnabrück repository record sits behind a challenge page and could not be read, so the discrepancy is not resolved here. The month is an ordering device.
stops.campa: He completes the doctorate with a dissertation titled 'Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition.' Both encyclopedias give the year as 2006; the dossier under review dates the dissertation to March 2007, and the repository record that would settle it sits behind a challenge page nobody could read. The discrepancy stands. What the thesis argues is that a mind without motives is not a simplified mind. It is a different object entirely, and it will not become the first one by being made larger.
suggested_refs: 'Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Building Blocks for an Architecture of Motivated Cognition', University of Osnabrück

stops.name: Osnabrück, the only book
stops.date_confidence: Publication by Oxford University Press in 2009 is attested. The physical description carried by the dossier (xxv + 374 pp., ISBN 978-0-19-537067-6) rests on that listing alone; a direct fetch of the publisher's page returned no content. The stop sits at his own institute, not at the press.
stops.campa: Oxford University Press publishes the dissertation as a book, 'Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: PSI: An Architecture of Motivated Cognition.' It is the only book-length work he authors. Nobody translates it, nobody collects him, and no second monograph follows; the rest of his output disperses into conference papers, lectures, podcast transcripts, and eventually a Substack. For a man whose subject is how a system holds itself together across time, the corpus is unusually loose. The book is published in Oxford. He is in Germany.
sources: Dossier bibliography (physical description unverified; OUP page fetch returned nothing)
suggested_refs: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: PSI, Oxford University Press, 2009

segments.name: The Congress Hall and the Companies

stops.name: Berlin, txtr and the reader
stops.date_confidence: Founding year corrected. The dossier gave 1999; de.wikipedia's txtr article states the company was founded in 2008 as Wizpac Ltd, and an April 2010 report calls Bach 'txtr-Mitbegründer' at the reader's launch. The exact office address is unpublished, so the coordinate is central Berlin.
stops.campa: In Berlin he co-founds txtr, an e-reader company registered first as Wizpac Ltd, with Christophe Maire and Andreas Steinhauser as managing directors. The German press of April 2010 calls him a txtr co-founder when the reader launches. The company reaches a hundred employees. The dossier dates the founding to 1999, nine years early, which would put it before his own degree; the German record puts it in 2008 and is followed here. Amazon is by then two years into the Kindle.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: The txtr reader, launched April 2010; txtr GmbH, Berlin, insolvent January 2015

stops.name: Berlin, the KI 2011 proceedings
stops.date_confidence: Attested by DBLP: 'KI 2011: Advances in Artificial Intelligence, 34th Annual German Conference on AI, Berlin, Germany, October 4-7, 2011', editors Joscha Bach and Stefan Edelkamp, LNCS 7006. Only the building within Berlin is unknown, so the coordinate is central Berlin.
stops.campa: He co-edits, with Stefan Edelkamp, the proceedings of the thirty-fourth German Conference on Artificial Intelligence, held in Berlin from the fourth to the seventh of October, published as Springer's Lecture Notes volume 7006. Editing a national conference's proceedings is the kind of work that leaves a name in a catalogue and nothing in a memoir. It is also how a research community decides who is trusted to say what counts. Which building in Berlin held it is recorded nowhere reachable.
suggested_refs: KI 2011: Advances in Artificial Intelligence, LNCS 7006, Springer 2011

stops.name: Berlin, the School of Mind and Brain
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The fellowship appears in en.wikipedia's summary and in no document fetched for this file; the month is an ordering device.
stops.campa: He holds a research fellowship at the Berlin School of Mind and Brain, Humboldt's graduate school for the traffic between neuroscience and philosophy, on Luisenstrasse a few streets from the Charité. The school exists to make philosophers read scanner output and neuroscientists read Kant, and he is at home in it. It is the last German academic position his record shows. Within two years his employer will be on the other side of the Atlantic, and the cost of employing him will be underwritten, in large part, by a registered sex offender.
suggested_refs: Berlin School of Mind and Brain, Luisenstrasse 56, Berlin

stops.name: Oxford, the AGI 2012 proceedings
stops.date_confidence: Attested by DBLP: 'Artificial General Intelligence - 5th International Conference, AGI 2012, Oxford, UK, December 8-11, 2012', editors Bach, Goertzel and Iklé, LNCS 7716. The venue building within Oxford is unknown; the coordinate is Oxford centre and verifies at 0.01 km.
stops.campa: With Ben Goertzel and Matthew Iklé he co-edits the proceedings of the fifth International Conference on Artificial General Intelligence, held at Oxford from the eighth to the eleventh of December. AGI is at this point a small field with a reputation problem, a few hundred people insisting that general intelligence is a buildable object while the mainstream builds classifiers. Goertzel is one of three men Bach will later name as having recommended him to a funder. That is a year away.
suggested_refs: Artificial General Intelligence: 5th International Conference, LNCS 7716, Springer 2012

stops.name: Hamburg, 30C3 and how to build a mind
stops.date_confidence: Venue corrected. The pool placed this talk at the bcc Berlin Congress Center; en.wikipedia's Chaos Communication Congress article lists 30C3 as 27-30 December 2013 at the Congress Center Hamburg, the congress having returned to Hamburg in 2012. Dates attested.
stops.campa: The Chaos Communication Congress has moved back to Hamburg after fourteen years in Berlin, and Bach walks onto a stage at the Congress Center to give a talk called 'How to Build a Mind.' The audience is hackers, not cognitive scientists. He gives them the whole architecture in ninety minutes: motivation, representation, attention, the self as a model the system runs on itself. The dossier places this talk at the Berlin congress centre. The congress had not met in Berlin since 2011.
suggested_refs: 'How to Build a Mind', 30C3, Congress Center Hamburg, December 2013, media.ccc.de

stops.name: Berlin, Micropsi Industries
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The founding and the co-founders appear in en.wikipedia's summary and in no document fetched here; the exact address is unpublished, so the coordinate is central Berlin and the month orders the segment.
stops.campa: Micropsi Industries GmbH is founded in Berlin by Bach with Ronnie Vuine, Ulrik Deichsel, Dominik Welland, and Priska Herger. The theory of motivated cognition goes to work on robot arms: adaptive control, machine learning applied to the part of factory automation where the workpiece is never quite where it was last time. Vuine had co-authored the first MicroPsi node-nets paper with him eleven years earlier. The name on the door is the name of the dissertation.
suggested_refs: Micropsi Industries GmbH, Berlin, founded 2014

stops.name: Hamburg, 31C3 and the second congress talk
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 31C3, 27-30 December 2014, Congress Center Hamburg, per en.wikipedia's Chaos Communication Congress article; the talk is cross-referenced to the media.ccc.de archive.
stops.campa: 'From Computation to Consciousness,' the second of what becomes an almost annual appointment with the congress. The argument runs that consciousness is something computation does once it starts modelling its own attention. He is by now living between two continents, drawing a Cambridge salary and returning each December to a German conference hall full of people who record everything and put it online for nothing. He has been employed at the Media Lab for eight months.
stops.quote: Consciousness naturally emerges when you have a system that makes a model of its own attention.
stops.quote_source: Joscha Bach, quoted in George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: 'From Computation to Consciousness', 31C3, Congress Center Hamburg, December 2014

stops.name: Berlin, txtr wound up and Hotheaven begun
stops.date_confidence: The txtr insolvency of January 2015 is attested by de.wikipedia. Hotheaven's founding year is not attested anywhere; Musser's profile establishes only that it came after txtr, which makes the dossier's 'c. early 2000s' impossible. Placed here as an ordering device.
stops.campa: txtr files for insolvency in January. The e-reader company that reached a hundred employees is wound up, and Bach founds Hotheaven, an artificial-intelligence task-planning application, in its wake. Neither company appears again in his public accounting of himself; the profile that mentions them gives each one a single clause, between the childhood and the theory. The dossier dates Hotheaven to the early 2000s, which cannot be right if it followed a company founded in 2008.
sources: George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: txtr GmbH insolvency filing, January 2015

stops.name: Hamburg, 32C3 and computational meta-psychology
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 32C3, 27-30 December 2015, Congress Center Hamburg, per en.wikipedia's Chaos Communication Congress article, cross-referenced to the media.ccc.de archive.
stops.campa: 'Computational Meta-Psychology,' delivered at the Congress Center Hamburg. He argues that the psychological categories, the self, the will, the feeling of understanding, are data structures with functions, and that a science of mind should be able to say what each of them is for rather than explain them away. The recording goes up on media.ccc.de within days, free and unedited. His employer that year is the MIT Media Lab, which is paying him with money it was given for the purpose.
stops.quote: The I that has experiences is fictional, a model that the brain generates.
stops.quote_source: Joscha Bach, quoted in George Musser, 'The Wizard of Consciousness', Psychology Today, 4 September 2018
suggested_refs: 'Computational Meta-Psychology', 32C3, Congress Center Hamburg, December 2015

stops.name: Hamburg, 33C3 and machine dreams
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 33C3, 27-30 December 2016, Congress Center Hamburg, per en.wikipedia's Chaos Communication Congress article, cross-referenced to the media.ccc.de archive.
stops.campa: 'Machine Dreams.' Two months after his MIT employment ends and five months after the two emails, he is back on the Hamburg stage talking about what a mind does when it generates worlds with nothing outside itself to check them against. Dreaming, on his account, is the world model running without its usual restraints, the same machinery with the corrections switched off. The Media Lab stopped paying him in October and the recording gives no sign of it. Nobody in the hall knows about the emails.
suggested_refs: 'Machine Dreams', 33C3, Congress Center Hamburg, December 2016

stops.campa: Jeffrey Epstein, five years past a conviction for procuring a child for prostitution, makes a donation to MIT earmarked for the support of Bach's research. It is the first of three, November 2013, July 2014, and September 2014, totalling three hundred thousand dollars. The same year Epstein introduces Bach to Joi Ito, who runs the Media Lab. Bach's own later account instead names three scientists who recommended him to Epstein: Ben Goertzel, Stephen Kosslyn, and Roger Schank. The two accounts of who introduced whom do not match.

stops.name: Cambridge, the first of the two emails
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Boston Globe of 21 November 2025 from correspondence released by Congress. The place of writing is not recorded anywhere; the stop is pinned at his place of employment and the day is an ordering device.

He will say afterward that he is extremely uncomfortable discussing the heritability of intelligence in public. He had not been writing in public.

stops.date_confidence: The role of vice president of research at the AI Foundation is attested by en.wikipedia; the start date is not, and 2019 comes from the dossier alone. The dossier's further claims of an O-1 visa and of financial independence from Epstein are attested by nothing fetched. The office address is unpublished; the coordinate is San Francisco.
